comparisons.peer_summary: Non-Markets net interest income is used to assess lending and deposit activities apart from Markets volatility, providing investors with an alternative view of underlying fundamentals and operational performance trends for these specific activities.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Citi disclose specific internal management measures related to net interest income from lending and deposit activities within their wealth or private banking contexts. GS describes 'Private banking and lending' revenues including net interest income from loans secured by assets and deposits raised from wealth management clients. Citi describes 'Non-Markets net interest income' used to assess lending, investing, and deposit-raising activities. While GS frames this as a business segment revenue source, Citi frames it as a non-GAAP performance metric to isolate fundamentals from Markets volatility, but both focus on the same core driver: interest income from client deposits and loans.

sentences.text: • Private banking and lending. Our private banking and lending activities include issuing loans to our wealth management clients. Such loans are generally secured by commercial and residential real estate, securities or other assets. We also raise deposits from wealth management clients, including through Marcus. Private banking and lending revenues include net interest income allocated to deposits and net interest income earned on loans to individual clients.

Management uses non-Markets net interest income to assess the performance of Citi's lending, investing (including asset-liability management) and deposit-raising activities, apart from any volatility associated with Markets activities.

comparisons.peer_summary: The business activities of Morgan Stanley's U.S. Bank Subsidiaries are generally limited to supporting its Institutional Securities and Wealth Management business segments.
